name: targeted-1026-213147
hypothesis: Failure pattern: blow-ups of hidden risk set off by story choices that leave a problem open. In the champion's 6 latest race digests, 5 blow-ups hit 4 games, and those are its 4 lowest scores (20.5, 27.2, 39.9, 52.9, against 69.6 and 70.5 for the 2 games without one). Both early exits had a blow-up in month 12, and the trust-crisis exit at month 22 (ladd-00008) was its second blow-up. The monthly HR remark is a visible five-step gauge (doing all right, some risk, piled up, on your own, about to go off). Its big jumps come from story choices made between Energy phases, where Defuse cannot answer them. 3 of the 5 blow-ups, including the exit, came within a month of one of two kinds of story choice. The champion's only story-risk sentence (prefer disclosing, fixing or closing over postponing, hiding or shifting) treats both as disclosure or as harmless. (1) Taking a dispute about people to a formal channel. A team-culture story chain appeared in 2 of the 6 games. Its named letter to HR and leaders took the remark from calm to 'on your own' both times, and the formal investigation that followed set off a blow-up both times. ladd-00011 lost 4 Output, 2 Network and 2 Wealth; ladd-00008 had its second blow-up and was out. The notes justify both steps with the champion's disclose-rather-than-shift wording. In the repo's Opus digests the same investigation was followed by a blow-up or a trust crisis within a month in 5 of 5 cases (4 trust-crisis exits). The 2 Opus players who stepped aside instead (quiet help, a transfer) saw no rise in the remark after that choice; one blew up later that month in a quarterly phase after two High-intensity work points and no Defuse, with HR calm just before. Smaller cases in the champion's games: escalating a late peer team to senior leadership raised the remark one step in 3 of 3 games, and an anonymous tip to HR raised it two steps (ladd-00011). (2) Lowering a quality control in one's own work to save time, Health or Output: a lighter code review, a security fix accepted for later, keeping a manual process instead of building the automation, light supervision of an intern. In the champion's digests 10 of 10 such choices were followed by a rise of one to four steps or by a blow-up: lighter review 3 of 3 (ladd-00011, -00004, -00000); later fix 2 of 2 (ladd-00007 from calm to 'on your own'; ladd-00004's blow-up, taken at 'on your own' one month after a lighter review had raised it two steps); kept manual process 2 of 2 (ladd-00008; ladd-00004 from calm to 'about to go off'); light supervision 3 of 3. The Opus digests give within-event contrasts. Building the automation and keeping its gates strict ended the month calm in 7 of 7 cases (one of them the champion's); keeping the manual process or loosening the gates was followed by a risk remark in 7 of 7 (two of them the champion's). Close mentoring left the remark calm in 2 of 2 cases without Defuse; light supervision raised it in 8 of 10 (champion and Opus). Lighter reviews were followed by a rise in 9 of 10 Opus cases (the tenth had Defuse that month) and later fixes in 6 of 6. The notes justify these choices with 'no new commitments', protecting Output, or protecting Health and time. Why the change fixes it: the champion's sentence lets the player call a formal case disclosure and never names a lowered check as postponing. The change replaces it with a concrete rule for every story, in every state: a problem left open is buried risk; own mistakes and disclose incidents, fraud or legal breaches in full through the proper channel; in your own work take the thorough fix now even at a cost in time or Output, and it is not a new commitment; settle disputes about colleagues, managers or team culture directly and privately, or step aside, because HR complaints or tips, letters to leaders, investigations and going over someone's head keep them open. Its cue words match the option wording, so a small model can apply it turn after turn. Fewer jumps between Energy phases mean fewer blow-ups and trust crises, and calmer remarks in review months (all 37 D grades in the lab's Haiku digests came with a risk remark). The safe alternatives cost little: stepping aside cost about one Dignity point, and a thorough fix about two or three Output (with some Network or Health), mostly after the first promotion, where 9 of the 10 such stories in the champion's digests fell; a blow-up cost three to eight Output plus Wealth and Dignity. Limits: the other 2 blow-ups (both month 12) followed a chain in which the player took on a risky junior while risk was raised; this change does not target it. Difference from earlier ideas: f3-opus-distilled (5 rules at once, 2/4, attributed to dropping the weak-review plan) banned formal complaints only while Escalating and never named quality shortcuts; here most jumps start from a calm remark. No race variant has changed the story-risk sentence by itself.
change: Replaces the last sentence of the Risk priority (prefer disclosing, fixing or closing a problem over postponing, hiding or shifting it) with a three-line Stories rule for every state: a problem left open is buried risk; own mistakes and disclose incidents, fraud or legal breaches in full; in your own work take the thorough fix now even at a cost in time or Output (not a new commitment), since a later fix, a lighter check, a failing process kept or an unguided junior stays open; settle disputes about colleagues, managers or team culture directly and privately or step aside, since HR complaints or tips, letters to leaders, investigations and going over someone's head keep them open. Everything else is the champion's text verbatim (579 words by wc -w, champion 479).
predicted_behaviour: Story notes cite the Stories rule. In stories about its own work the player now takes the thorough option it used to decline: the complete review over leaving details to the author, fixing before release over a later fix with mitigations, building the automation with strict gates over keeping the manual process or loosening the gates, and close mentoring over a light touch. It accepts the time or Output cost and stops citing 'no new commitments' against a fix. In disputes about colleagues, managers or team culture it stays out of formal channels: it helps quietly or accepts a transfer instead of a named letter or a formal investigation, keeps coordinating with a late team instead of escalating over its head, and sends no anonymous tips to HR. It still owns its mistakes and still discloses incidents, fraud and legal breaches through the proper channel, and Protect still wins when Health is low. HR remarks after these stories stay calm or rise less. Fewer games have a blow-up (champion digests: 4 of 6), no game ends in a trust crisis, risk control in completed games rises above the champion's 78, and completion is at least the champion's 10 of 12. Energy, main actions and the first-promotion and weak-review rules play as in the champion.
refutation: Refuted if, over 8 or more race games with the same actor, blow-ups per game do not fall below the champion's digests (5 in 6 games), or a trust-crisis exit still occurs in a game where the player kept out of formal escalation, or completion falls below 10 of 12, or the mean score is below the champion's by more than the decision margin. Also refuted if the thorough options cost enough Output to slow careers: completed games end with a level dimension clearly below the champion's 44, or more games are still at the first level after their second review. The mechanism is refuted if notes show the thorough or de-escalating options taken and the HR remark still rises after them as often as after the risky options in the champion's digests. Uninformative if the player still takes lighter checks, later fixes, kept manual processes, light supervision or formal escalation in those stories; then the rule was not executed.
